response:
- Claude A's finding is real and I confirm it: `UI/Components/ShareSheet.swift` (my new file this round) isn't in `project.pbxproj` yet — TodayScreen's reference to `ShareSheet`/`SharePayload` will fail to compile until the integrator runs `xcodegen generate`. This is a hard precondition before the next build attempt, same class of bug as the `BootstrapRecipeBuilder` saga.
- Codex B's `Services/Purchases/StoreManager.swift` is a duplicate of my already-real, already-tested `Services/StoreKit/StoreKitManager.swift` (wired into `SettingsScreen.swift`, covered by `Tests/StoreKitManagerTests.swift`) — exact repeat of the wrong-lane pattern banned in prior rounds. Must not land.
- Codex B's plan to "update SettingsScreen.swift to include purchase and restore buttons" would collide with my already-shipped, fully-wired purchase/restore UI in that file (real price lookup, three-state restore outcome, notification row). Nothing there needs building.
- Codex B's `WatermarkOverlay.swift`/`MetadataScrubber.swift` duplicate work my `ExportPipeline.swift` already does: watermarking is the renderer's job per DEC-prompt_contract-010 (composited by `AuraRenderer`, guaranteed non-overlapping with focal art/caption), and EXIF/GPS stripping is already handled by `ExportPipeline.pngData` (no metadata dictionary attached at all, tested in `Tests/ExportPipelineTests.swift`). A second post-hoc UIGraphics overlay can't honor that non-overlap guarantee and shouldn't exist alongside the renderer contract.
- `WatermarkOverlay.apply`'s posted code also `fatalError()`s if the bundled asset is missing — a crash path, not acceptable regardless of duplication.
- Codex B's plan to add "a local .storekit configuration file" would recreate the previously-banned duplicate-`.storekit`-config pattern — `Aura.storekit` already exists and is wired into `project.yml`'s scheme.
- Net: integrator should drop `StoreManager.swift`, `WatermarkOverlay.swift`, `MetadataScrubber.swift`, and any second `.storekit` file if they land, and run `xcodegen generate` to pick up my legitimate `ShareSheet.swift`.
